prompts.grotesque:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: an original fine-art illustration study for an interactive Shanhaijing website, one of two proposed visual directions, not a reproduction of a historical image.
Subject: Zhuyin (烛阴), the deity below Zhong Mountain from the Classic of Mountains and Seas, described as human-faced, serpent-bodied, red in color, immense enough to span the landscape. Exactly one creature with one clearly human face and one long continuous snake body. No arms, no legs, no antlers, no dragon whiskers, no wings.
Style direction A — archaic grotesque bestiary: uncanny and strange, austere and slightly disturbing rather than cute, monumental twisting anatomy, sharply intelligent old human face with wide unblinking eyes that is organically connected to the snake neck, not a separate portrait pasted onto it. Obsessive irregular hand-drawn black scale marks and ancient woodcut-like contour lines, weathered mineral cinnabar red washes, soot-black dry ink, muted bone parchment. Dense but masterfully controlled tactile brushwork, wormlike coils threading angular old mountains, a little smoky void. The face should feel mysterious and non-modern, not handsome fantasy concept art. Shape and anatomical silhouette are the focus. Ancient Chinese strange-tales atmosphere without reproducing a named artist.
Composition: nearly square museum-quality illustration, whole sinuous body visible as a readable strong silhouette, generous parchment margins around it, creature large enough to read at 300px, loose rocky ground beneath, no frame, no typography, no seal, no captions or watermark. No blood or gore, no neon, no shiny 3D, no anime, no generic European dragon. Paper background should be off-white and aged naturally. Image must be powerful as a single artwork; do not make a collage or interface.
prompts.ink:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: original Chinese ink-and-mineral-pigment painting for a Shanhaijing reading website; contemporary artistic interpretation, not a historical reconstruction.
Subject: Zhuyin (烛阴), the ancient deity described as human-faced, serpent-bodied, red in color, immense enough to span a mountain landscape. Exactly one clearly human face attached organically to one single long continuous serpentine body. No arms, legs, wings, horns, or dragon whiskers.
Style direction C — expansive ink wash: elegant, poetic, otherworldly but retaining real strangeness. Bold expressive calligraphic serpent body built from varied broken dry-brush marks and pools of diluted ink; very restrained dark cinnabar mineral wash running along its body. A small but unmistakably human face, solemn and strange, looking back toward the viewer; no smiling mascot. Creature uncoils between distant low mountains and mist so that the sweep of the body suggests wind and time. Real hand-brushed transitions between wet ink bleed, dry brush, pale grey wash and untouched warm xuan paper. Sparse, confident, irregular brushwork with variation in edge softness; not traced outlines, not a clean vector icon, not photorealistic.
Composition: nearly square standalone fine-art painting, ample breathable unpainted paper, around half negative space, whole creature and implied mountain-scale length readable at thumbnail size; a few distant mountain marks and very spare vegetation only. Delicate quiet paper texture, no brown grunge vignette. No written characters, no title, no stamps, no interface, no framing, no watermark. No extra creatures, no luminous magic effects, no 3D and no generic fantasy dragon. This sample must have a visibly lighter, more spacious composition than a dense grotesque woodcut.
